transcript: There are days when I wake up and I wonder who I am and what got me to this point.
Does your mom ever wonder where she went wrong?
I didn't want to go places because I didn't want to have to deal with the people's looks, the people judging me.
My outside appearance has never changed my inside appearance.
I'm Jeff Hanks. I'm 24 years old and I got my first tattoo when I was 18.
Tattoo artists will even tell people, well don't get it on your neck.
You know, you only have a few, so why go for your neck or your knuckles or your hands?
Because that's like prime real estate right there. That's what's going to stand out.
You could cover it up with like long sleeves every day.
It's out there, you know. You've got to find something that will accept you.
Every day is a struggle, you know. It's what people think of you.
What does an average person that comes through, like that runs into me, think of me?
The difference is obviously I stand out more.
But what are you thinking when I'm walking by you?
Am I going to snatch your jacket?
Am I going to take your child away from you?
Or do you think I'm going to rob this place?
My family kind of, it took a long time for them to accept this is my lifestyle now, you know.
I can't make these go away. These don't disappear.
Tattoos can be an addiction.
Maybe not addicted to the pain.
Addicted to the outcome of the artwork.
And knowing that you're sitting there and bonding with this person for six or seven hours.
And you're getting something amazing out of it.
You learn so much about them.
You learn so much about the trade too.
You learn so much about the tattooed world.
There is so much to tattooing that society doesn't know.
Just the biggest pet peeve is people's ignorance.
People talking and saying,
Wow, you have a lot of tattoos.
And what do your parents think?
Or what are you going to do later in life?
Or, you know, how much money do you have invested?
I have the 1927 and my grandmother's initials, which were F and D.
And I was really close to my grandparents.
I have buttons on both my thumbs.
And it kind of just all goes together when I put my hands together if I was praying.
And I think that's just my favorite piece out of all the big pieces that I have.
Even though it's so small, it just really means something.
Much a business card for different artists because people will approach me and ask me where I get my artwork done.
I think I've counted and I've had over 13 different artists work on me.
It's slowly changing, but it's going to take a long time for the world to accept.
